# ngrok documentation: Integrations

> Every page in the Integrations section of the ngrok docs (150 pages). Each link points to the page's Markdown version.

## Integrations

- [Integrations Hub](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/index.md): Find guides for using ngrok with identity providers, webhook senders, logging tools, Kubernetes platforms, and other third-party services.

## General Guides

- [How to Access Home Assistant from Anywhere with ngrok](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/guides/home-assistant-with-ngrok.md): Run Home Assistant in Docker and put it online with ngrok, so you can open your smart home dashboard from outside your network.
- [MQTT](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/guides/mqtt.md): Learn how to expose your MQTT server to the internet using ngrok TCP tunnels and connect remotely with MQTT Explorer.
- [Expose Local Services Behind CGNAT Without Port Forwarding](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/cgnat.md): Behind CGNAT on Starlink or T-Mobile Home Internet? Use ngrok to reach local apps, SSH, and servers without port forwarding or router access.
- [Configuring GoDaddy DNS for ngrok Reserved Domains](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/godaddy.md): Step-by-step guide for configuring GoDaddy DNS records to work with ngrok reserved domains using CNAME records.
- [Using ngrok with Google Colab](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/googleColab.md): Install pyngrok in a Google Colab notebook, add your authtoken, and start a tunnel to a service running in the notebook.
- [Using ngrok with Java](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/java.md): Learn how to use ngrok with Java applications using the ngrok Java SDK or API client for programmatic account management.
- [Using ngrok with Minecraft](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/minecraft.md): Learn how to share your Minecraft server with others using ngrok TCP endpoints, including free plan limitations and troubleshooting tips.
- [Using ngrok with OpenVPN Connect](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/openvpn.md): Run an OpenVPN server behind CGNAT by putting it on an ngrok TCP endpoint and pointing your .ovpn profile at that address.
- [Using ngrok with Puppet](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/puppet.md): Learn how to use the ngrok Puppet module to install and configure ngrok resources and ensure the agent process is running.
- [Using ngrok with Visual Studio / IIS Express](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/visualStudio.md): Install the ngrok extension for Visual Studio, connect it to your account, and start a tunnel to a site running in IIS Express.
- [Using ngrok with VSCode](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/vsCode.md): Learn how to use the ngrok VSCode extension to add ngrok support directly into your VSCode development environment.

## General Guides / Docker

- [Using ngrok with Docker](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/docker/index.md): Run the ngrok agent from its official Docker image and use it to put apps in other containers or on your host machine online.
- [Using ngrok with Docker Compose](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/docker/compose.md): This example shows how to run the ngrok agent alongside your services in Docker Compose, using an ngrok.yml file to define the endpoints.
- [Using ngrok Docker Desktop](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/docker/desktop.md): Install the ngrok extension in Docker Desktop and use it to put any of your running containers online from the Docker Desktop UI.

## CLI Credentials

- [How to Secure Your ngrok CLI Credentials with 1Password](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/cli-credentials/1password.md): Keep your ngrok authtoken in 1Password instead of ngrok.yml, and load it automatically with the 1Password shell plugin.

## Dashboard SSO

- [Configure Auth0 Single Sign-On with SAML](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/dashboard-sso/auth0-dashboard-sso-saml.md): Create a SAML application in Auth0 and connect it to your ngrok account, so teammates use their Auth0 logins to reach the ngrok dashboard.
- [Microsoft Entra ID SSO (SAML)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/dashboard-sso/microsoft-sso-saml.md): Let your team sign in to the ngrok dashboard with their Microsoft Entra ID accounts by setting up SAML single sign-on for your ngrok account.
- [Configure Okta Single Sign-On (SSO) Using OpenID Connect (OIDC)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/dashboard-sso/okta-dashboard-sso-oidc.md): Let your team sign in to the ngrok dashboard with their Okta accounts by setting up OpenID Connect single sign-on for your ngrok account.
- [Configure Okta Single Sign-On (SSO)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/dashboard-sso/okta-dashboard-sso-saml.md): Let your team sign in to the ngrok dashboard with their Okta accounts by setting up SAML single sign-on for your ngrok account.
- [Automate User Provisioning via SCIM with Okta](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/dashboard-sso/okta-dashboard-sso-scim.md): Connect Okta to your ngrok account with SCIM, so users you add or remove in Okta are added to or removed from ngrok automatically.
- [Salesforce Dashboard Single Sign-On (SSO) Using OIDC](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/dashboard-sso/salesforce-dashboard-sso-oidc.md): Use Salesforce's managed applications to add single sign-on (SSO) for your ngrok dashboard using the OIDC integration.

## Databases

- [Using ngrok with MySQL](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/mysql.md): Open a TCP endpoint on port 3306 with ngrok so you can connect to a MySQL database on your machine from another network.
- [Using ngrok with MongoDB](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/mongodb.md): Reach a MongoDB server on your machine from another network through an ngrok TCP endpoint, and connect to it with a client.
- [Using ngrok with PostgreSQL](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/postgresql.md): Open a TCP endpoint on port 5432 with ngrok so you can connect to a PostgreSQL database on your machine from another network.
- [Using ngrok with Redis](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/redis.md): Protect your Redis server first, then open an ngrok TCP endpoint on port 6379 so you can reach it from another network.

## Endpoints SSO

- [Auth0 Endpoint SSO (OpenID Connect)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/auth0-sso-oidc.md): Make visitors sign in with Auth0 before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using an OpenID Connect app and a Traffic Policy.
- [Azure Active Directory B2C SSO (SAML)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/azure-sso-saml.md): Make visitors sign in with Microsoft Azure AD B2C before they reach your ngrok endpoints, using a SAML app and a Traffic Policy.
- [Secure Your Endpoints with Curity Identity Server SSO (OpenID Connect)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/curity-sso-oidc.md): Make visitors sign in with Curity before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using an OpenID Connect app and a Traffic Policy.
- [Secure Your Endpoints with Descope SSO (OpenID Connect)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/descope-sso-oidc.md): Make visitors sign in with Descope before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using an OpenID Connect app and a Traffic Policy.
- [Secure Your Endpoints with Descope SSO (SAML)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/descope-sso-saml.md): Make visitors sign in with Descope before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using a SAML app and a Traffic Policy.
- [Secure Your Endpoints with Frontegg SSO (OpenID Connect)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/frontegg-sso-oidc.md): Make visitors sign in with Frontegg before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using an OpenID Connect app and a Traffic Policy.
- [Secure Your Endpoints with Frontegg SSO (SAML)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/frontegg-sso-saml.md): Make visitors sign in with Frontegg before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using a SAML app and a Traffic Policy.
- [FusionAuth Endpoint SSO (OpenID Connect)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/fusionauth-sso-oidc.md): Make visitors sign in with FusionAuth before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using an OpenID Connect app and a Traffic Policy.
- [JumpCloud Endpoint SSO (OpenID Connect)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/jumpcloud-sso-oidc.md): Make visitors sign in with JumpCloud before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using an OpenID Connect app and a Traffic Policy.
- [JumpCloud SSO (SAML)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/jumpcloud-sso-saml.md): Make visitors sign in with JumpCloud before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using a SAML app and a Traffic Policy.
- [miniOrange Endpoint SSO (OpenID Connect)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/miniorange-sso-oidc.md): Make visitors sign in with miniOrange before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using an OpenID Connect app and a Traffic Policy.
- [miniOrange SSO (SAML)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/miniorange-sso-saml.md): Make visitors sign in with miniOrange before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using a SAML app and a Traffic Policy.
- [Secure Your Endpoints with Okta SSO (OpenID Connect)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/okta-sso-oidc.md): Make visitors sign in with Okta before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using an OpenID Connect app and a Traffic Policy.
- [Secure Your Endpoints with Okta SSO (SAML)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/okta-sso-saml.md): Make visitors sign in with Okta before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using a SAML app and a Traffic Policy.
- [Secure ngrok Endpoints Using Salesforce OpenID Connect](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/salesforce-sso-oidc.md): Make visitors sign in with Salesforce before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using an external client app and the OIDC action.
- [Wallix Trustelem Endpoint SSO (OpenID Connect)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/trustelem-sso-oidc.md): Make visitors sign in with Wallix Trustelem before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using an OpenID Connect app and a Traffic Policy.
- [Wallix Trustelem SSO (SAML)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/endpoint-sso/trustelem-sso-saml.md): Make visitors sign in with Wallix Trustelem before they can reach your ngrok endpoints, using a SAML app and a Traffic Policy.

## Event Destinations

- [Send Network Logs from ngrok to AWS CloudWatch](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/event-destinations/amazon-cloudwatch-event-destination.md): Export ngrok events, such as traffic logs and account changes, to an AWS CloudWatch log group for monitoring and auditing.
- [Send Network Logs from ngrok to AWS Firehose](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/event-destinations/amazon-firehose-event-destination.md): Export ngrok events, such as traffic logs and account changes, to an AWS Firehose delivery stream for monitoring and auditing.
- [Send Network Logs from ngrok to AWS Kinesis](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/event-destinations/amazon-kinesis-event-destination.md): Export ngrok events, such as traffic logs and account changes, to an AWS Kinesis data stream for monitoring and auditing.
- [Integrate with the Azure Logs Ingestion API](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/event-destinations/azure-logs-event-destination.md): Export ngrok events, such as traffic logs and account changes, to an Azure Log Analytics workspace through the Logs Ingestion API.
- [Send Network Logs from ngrok to Datadog](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/event-destinations/datadog-event-destination.md): Export ngrok events, such as traffic logs and account changes, to Datadog so you can search, monitor, and alert on them.

## Frameworks

- [Using ngrok with FastAPI](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/fastAPI.md): Start an ngrok endpoint from inside a FastAPI app with the ngrok-python library, using library versions that are known to work together.
- [Using ngrok with Flask](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/flask.md): Share a Flask development server through ngrok, either by running the ngrok agent next to it or by starting ngrok from the Python SDK.
- [Using ngrok with Laravel](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/laravel.md): Laravel Valet has ngrok support built in. Learn how to add your ngrok authtoken to Valet so it can put your local Laravel sites online.

## JWT Validation

- [Enable JWT Validation with Auth0](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/jwt-validation/auth0.md): Configure the jwt-validation Traffic Policy action to accept only requests that carry a valid access token issued by Auth0.

## Kubernetes Ingress

- [Kubernetes Ingress Integrations](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/index.md): Find guides for running the ngrok Kubernetes Operator on cloud providers like EKS, cluster management tools like Rancher, and service meshes.
- [Deploy a Production API and Gateway with APIOps Using Argo CD and ngrok](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/apiops.md): Deploy an API and its gateway policies to Kubernetes from one Git repository, using Argo CD and the ngrok Kubernetes Operator.
- [Ingress to Apps Secured by Microsoft Entra ID in Kubernetes](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/azure-ad-k8s.md): Require a Microsoft Entra ID login for a Kubernetes app by adding SAML to its Traffic Policy in the ngrok Kubernetes Operator.
- [Ingress to Kubernetes Apps Deployed on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/azure-aks-k8s.md): Add public ingress to an app running on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) using ngrok's Kubernetes Operator, then secure it with Traffic Policy.
- [Kubernetes Ingress to Services in a Consul Service Mesh](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/consul-k8s.md): Route public traffic to services in a Consul service mesh on Kubernetes with the ngrok Kubernetes Operator, then add OAuth.
- [Ingress to Kubernetes Apps on Clusters Managed by DigitalOcean](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/digitalocean-k8s.md): Add Kubernetes ingress to any app running in a cluster managed by DigitalOcean using the ngrok Kubernetes Operator.
- [Kubernetes Ingress to Services Hosted on EKS](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/eks.md): Install the ngrok Kubernetes Operator on an AWS EKS cluster, put a sample app online, and protect it with Traffic Policy.
- [ngrok External Secrets Integration](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/external-secrets.md): Store API keys and other credentials as Kubernetes secrets, then use the External Secrets Operator to make them available to ngrok.
- [Kubernetes Ingress to GKE Services with ngrok](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/google-kubernetes-engine.md): Learn how to use the ngrok Kubernetes Operator on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) to quickly add secure Kubernetes ingress to your apps or APIs.
- [Use ngrok's Global Server Load Balancing with DigitalOcean](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/gslb.md): Layer load balancing between three or more globally distributed, cloud-based virtual machines in DigitalOcean using ngrok's GSLB.
- [Ingress to a Microservices-Based Application Connected via Linkerd's Service Mesh](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/k8s.md): Use Linkerd and the ngrok Kubernetes Operator together, so a meshed microservices app gets public ingress while Linkerd handles mTLS inside it.
- [Kubernetes Ingress to Apps/APIs on Clusters Managed by Canonical MicroK8s](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/microk8s-k8s.md): Add ingress to any app running in a Kubernetes cluster managed by Canonical MicroK8s using the ngrok Kubernetes Operator.
- [Ingress to Kubernetes Apps Managed by Rafay](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/rafay-k8s.md): Install the ngrok Kubernetes Operator on a cluster managed by Rafay, optionally as a blueprint, and put a demo app online.
- [Kubernetes Ingress to Applications and Clusters Managed by Rancher](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/rancher-k8s.md): Set up an RKE2 cluster with Rancher and route public traffic to a sample app on it with the ngrok Kubernetes Operator.
- [Ingress to Kubernetes Apps Deployed on Spectro Cloud Palette](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/spectro-cloud-k8s.md): Deploy the ngrok Kubernetes Operator with a Spectro Cloud Palette cluster profile and route public traffic to an example app.
- [Ingress to Kubernetes Apps and Services with vcluster](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/kubernetes-ingress/vcluster-k8s.md): Route public traffic to an app in a vcluster virtual cluster with the ngrok Kubernetes Operator, then protect it with OAuth.

## OAuth

- [Facebook OAuth](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/oauth/facebook-oauth.md): Create a Facebook app and use it with the ngrok oauth action, so visitors sign in with Facebook before they reach your endpoint.
- [GitHub OAuth](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/oauth/github-oauth.md): Create a GitHub OAuth app and use it with the ngrok oauth action, so visitors sign in with GitHub before they reach your endpoint.
- [GitLab OAuth](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/oauth/gitlab-oauth.md): Create a GitLab application and use it with the ngrok oauth action, so visitors sign in with GitLab before they reach your endpoint.
- [Google OAuth](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/oauth/google-oauth.md): Configure ngrok to authenticate users with Google OAuth 2.0. Set up a GCP project, consent screen, and OAuth client.
- [LinkedIn OAuth](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/oauth/linkedin-oauth.md): Configure ngrok to authenticate users with LinkedIn OAuth. Create an app in the LinkedIn Developer Portal and set the callback URL.
- [Microsoft OAuth](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/oauth/microsoft-oauth.md): Configure ngrok to authenticate users with Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) OAuth. Register an app in the Azure portal.
- [Amazon OAuth](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/oauth/oauth.md): Create a Login with Amazon security profile and use it with the ngrok oauth action, so visitors sign in with Amazon first.
- [Twitch OAuth](https://ngrok.com/docs/integrations/oauth/twitch-oauth.md): Configure ngrok to authenticate users with Twitch OAuth. Register an application in the Twitch developer console.

## Protocols

- [Using ngrok with SSH](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/ssh.md): Learn how to use ngrok TCP endpoints to access your local SSH server remotely on port 22 with proper port specification.
- [Using ngrok with FTP, FTPS, SFTP](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/ftp.md): Learn how to use ngrok with SFTP for secure file transfers, and why FTP/FTPS are not recommended due to multiple port requirements.
- [Using ngrok with Websockets](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/websockets.md): This example shows how to serve WebSocket and HTTP traffic from one local port through a single ngrok HTTP endpoint, with no extra configuration.
- [Using ngrok with Real-Time Messaging Protocol (RTMP)](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/rtmp.md): Learn how to share your RTMP streaming server using ngrok TCP endpoints on port 1935 for live video streaming.

## Web Servers

- [Using ngrok with SMTP Mail Servers](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/smtp.md): Reach a mail server on your machine from another network by forwarding SMTP over an ngrok TCP endpoint on port 25, 465, 587, or 2525.
- [Using ngrok with NGINX](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/nginx.md): Learn how to use ngrok with NGINX by setting the host header flag to properly route requests to your virtual hosts.
- [Using ngrok with an Outbound Proxy](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/outboundProxy.md): Learn how to configure ngrok to work through HTTP or SOCKS5 outbound proxies using environment variables or configuration files.
- [Using ngrok with Virtual Hosts Like MAMP and WAMP](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/virtualHosts.md): Point an ngrok endpoint at a MAMP or WAMP install that serves several local sites, and make sure each visitor reaches the one you intended.
- [Using ngrok with gRPC](https://ngrok.com/docs/using-ngrok-with/gRPC.md): Put a gRPC service online with ngrok by forwarding over HTTP/2 from an HTTPS endpoint, or by using a TCP endpoint instead.
